text: Armaz Akhvlediani - The government supported Metropolitan Shio, this is crystal clear; it was and is involved - we saw this and I suspect we will see it even before the start of the historic Synod, where the Patriarch is to be elected (28.04.2026, 19:37)

"It is possible that for the final session, where the Synod must elect the Patriarch, the configuration may change to some extent—Metropolitan Shio has advanced, but I would not rush and would not draw a final conclusion," politician Armaz Akhvlediani stated on the PalitraNews program "Resume."
According to Armaz Akhvlediani, everything will depend on where the votes of the remaining two candidates go.

"The main decision is still ahead; today the Synod session only selected candidates. We already know the data on who received how many votes. Let us also not forget that for the final session, where the Synod is to elect the Patriarch, it is not out of the question that the configuration may change to some extent. However, it is clear today who has taken the lead—Metropolitan Shio has taken the lead—but unlike others, I would not rush to make a final conclusion."

"Today, the Patriarch was not being elected; only three candidates were nominated today, and when one is to be selected, the other two may agree on where their votes, as well as those of others, will go," stated Armaz Akhvlediani.
According to Armaz Akhvlediani, it is crystal clear that the government is interfering in the patriarchal elections and supports Metropolitan Shio.

“The government supported Metropolitan Shio; this is as clear as day. It was and is involved. Let’s say it directly: all pro-government media, from morning till night, actively, in every context, regardless of the topic they were discussing, directly or indirectly supported this one candidate. If this is not interference, then what is?! As for interference by other means, I cannot speak on that; I do not have a single fact—if I had, I would say so. But I have a reasonable suspicion and assumption that a wicked government at all times has levers of impact, influence, and pressure—especially a government whose authority is destroyed and needs to cling to something, in this case, the church's authority maintained by inertia, and use it for its own benefit. We have seen this during this time, and I suspect we will see it even before the start of the historic Synod, where the final Patriarch is to be chosen,” stated Armaz Akhvlediani.

For information, the Holy Synod has selected three patriarchal candidates. By the decision of the Synod, the candidates for the patriarchate will be: the Locum Tenens of the Patriarchal Throne, Metropolitan Shio (Mujiri) of Senaki and Chkhorotsqu, Metropolitan Iobi of the Urbnisi and Ruisi Eparchy, and Metropolitan Grigoli of Poti and Khobi.

As the head of the Public Relations Service of the Patriarchate, Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, told journalists, the Locum Tenens of the Patriarchal Throne, Shio, received 20 votes, while the other two candidates received 7 votes each. Furthermore, according to his explanation, the other candidates were Metropolitan Grigol Katsia, Metropolitan Dositheos, and Metropolitan Melchizedek.
